title: Which entity is the test about?
hook: Compare row reuse with a genuinely unseen entity.

doesNotKnow: A rows have label 0; B rows label 1. An entity-lookup predictor trained only on A defaults unknown IDs to 0. How many of two held-out B rows are correct?

objective: Compute the group split leakage finite model and explain its changed countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text:
29. group-split-leakage

Target / packet: ai-group-split-leakage · F2. Prerequisites: ai:data-leakage.

Nearest / distinct payoff: data-leakage → duplicates-in-the-test. General leakage has many causes; this isolates duplicate entity identity crossing splits and specifies which deployment target the split evaluates.

Finite primary model: Two entities A/B each have 2 duplicate feature rows with labels A 0/B 1. Row-split train A 1, B 1 and test A 2, B 2 lets entity lookup score 2/2. Entity-split train only A, test only B makes unknown fallback 0 score 0/2.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: A declared transferable feature equals target lets rule predictor score 2/2 even on heldout B. Group disjointness is needed for new entity evaluation, not proof all row-splits leak for every deployment target.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict lookup score on unseen entity; recall which test matches returning-entity versus new-entity deployment.

Required observable evidence: Show explicit entity IDs and row membership; count real heldout outcomes, not just split colors.

Source obligation: Declared local finite model. Exact results require independent arithmetic reproduction; this construction supports no real-model performance or universal improvement claim. Method-source obligations remain as listed in the acquisition record below.
